learningObjectives: Describe Channels, Portals, landing pages, and dashboards in Pega Constellation applications.
Configure out-of-the-box widgets, themes, and the Enterprise layer for branding and reuse.

topics.title: Themes and styles for Constellation applications

elements.text: Think of a Portal as a web entrance to an office, not a separate building beneath every Channel. Landing pages are rooms and Widgets provide their useful equipment. A shared design system helps selected applications reuse the organization’s visual identity; themes require sharing or copying rather than automatic inheritance.

elements.description: A Channel allows you to create tailored interactive UIs for specific interaction types. Examples: messaging service, voice service, web portal, mobile portal. Channels are created from templates with predefined layouts and navigation.

Facebook Messenger, WhatsApp, Apple Messages, SMS/MMS (Twilio), Embedded chat window, Amazon Alexa, Email. IVA (Intelligent Virtual Assistant): understands user intent across channels. Email Bot: auto-detects email intent and routes.

Create, view, and edit all Channel interfaces from one place. Download additional Channels from Pega Marketplace. Lock icon on a Channel = the Channel component has NOT yet been added to the application (not a permission restriction).

Drafting Persona-Channel associations in the Case Life Cycle does not configure access. The source describes all pages as the default for a Persona; restrict the appropriate Portal through Portal configuration, rather than assuming lifecycle labels grant or restrict access.

elements.description: A Portal is a web Channel that supports browser access on desktop and mobile. Choose a Portal type for the user profile; use configured privileges and visibility in one Portal, or provide separate Portals.
items: Standard work Portals: for professional users completing complex, recurring workflows requiring collaboration and data analysis
Self-service Portals: minimalistic design with a guided experience for simple, goal-oriented tasks

elements.description: Consolidate Case-related information. Contain data lists, Widgets, Views, and Insights. Out-of-the-box pages: Dashboard, Home, Explore Data, My Work, Self-service Main page. Landing pages added to the Portal menu appear in Portal navigation.

4 templates: Default page (column-based with/without banner), Tabbed page, Dashboard page, Inline Dashboard page. The Default page supports both column-based layout and dynamic layout (drag, drop, and resize widgets).

elements.caption: A Portal is a web Channel, not a child of every Channel type. Dashboards are landing pages with region-organized Widgets.

elements.description: Dashboard = a landing page accessed in the Portal. Contains Widgets that consolidate summary info and KPIs. A Template divides the work area into Regions (containers for widgets). Each Persona gets a tailored dashboard view.

items: Private: only the creator sees it
Shared — Users with Access: all users or a specific Access Group
Public: all users in the application
bulletPoints: Creating a NEW dashboard → default = Private
COPYING an existing dashboard → new dashboard INHERITS the source's visibility

elements.description: Widgets appear in two places: Portal landing pages AND Full Case View (Utilities pane). The Utilities pane is HIDDEN when no Widgets are added — it doesn't show an empty state.
The v3 topic lists these Portal Widget examples:
items: Pulse: team collaboration (posts, comments, attachments) — available in landing pages AND Full Case View
To do: configurable to show My Worklist, team members, or Work Queue
App announcement: custom welcome text + link

elements.description: The source’s Home example contains Pulse, To do and App announcement. Do not treat this illustration as a guarantee that every configured Portal has the same defaults.

The source lists Attachments, Case operator, Tags, GenAI Coach, Followers, Prediction, Stakeholders and Related Cases as Utilities examples. Pulse is also supported in the Full Case View. This is not an exhaustive support matrix.

elements.description: Pegasus, Aries, Self-Service, Bootes. MUST SAVE UNDER A NEW NAME before customizing any of them — you cannot edit the original built-in themes directly. Configure at App Studio → Settings → Themes. The Themes landing page also provides accessibility configurations.

The source also calls the Enterprise layer a COE layer. Reuse shared themes, fonts, icons and templates across applications. UI elements can be inherited, but themes do not support inheritance: share high-level design tokens, or save a specialized theme copy into a higher Ruleset.

Store component styling in one central place. The system auto-generates platform-specific styling from those tokens, ensuring visual consistency across mobile, desktop, and other surfaces. All Constellation library components use design tokens.

Tokens generate platform-specific styling.</text></svg>
elements.caption: Shared design-system reuse does not mean themes inherit. Design tokens drive platform-specific styling, not generated tokens.

examPitfalls.title: Persona-Channel in Case lifecycle ≠ Channel access configuration
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Case lifecycle Persona-Channel labels describe the design; they do not configure access. Review the Portal configuration rather than assuming a stage label restricts users.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Drafting Persona-Channel associations in the Case lifecycle does NOT configure Channel access. By default, a Persona has access to ALL pages. Channel access is configured separately in the Portal configuration.

examPitfalls.title: Lock icon on Channel = component not added — not a permission lock
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The Channels landing-page lock indicates that the component has not been added to the application. It is not an administrator-only or edit-permission marker.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A Lock icon on a Channel indicates the Channel component has not yet been added to the application — not a permission restriction or edit lock.

examPitfalls.title: New dashboard default = Private; copy inherits source visibility
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask what visibility a copied dashboard receives. Candidates answer 'Private' because new dashboards default to Private — not realizing a COPIED dashboard inherits the source dashboard's visibility setting.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Creating a NEW dashboard → defaults to Private. COPYING an existing dashboard → new dashboard inherits the source dashboard's visibility.

examPitfalls.title: Not all Access Groups have Personas
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask whether configuring a Persona is required before granting access via an Access Group. Candidates say yes. Access Groups can be configured and assigned without any linked Persona — Personas are optional mappings that help organize role definitions.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Creating a Persona in App Studio auto-creates an Access Group in Dev Studio. The reverse is NOT true — not all Access Groups have corresponding Personas in App Studio.

examPitfalls.title: Ready-to-use themes must be saved under a new name before customizing
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks how to modify the Pegasus theme. Candidates describe editing it directly. All four built-in themes (Pegasus, Aries, Self-Service, Bootes) are locked — you must save a copy under a new name first.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Built-in themes must be SAVED UNDER A NEW NAME before they can be customized. You cannot directly edit the original four built-in themes.

examPitfalls.title: Enterprise reuse does not mean theme inheritance
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The source also calls the Enterprise layer a COE layer, but explicitly says themes do not support inheritance.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Share the Enterprise design system; save application-specific theme copies into a higher Ruleset when specialization is needed.

examPitfalls.title: Utilities pane is HIDDEN when empty — no placeholder shown
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask what the user sees in the Utilities pane when no widgets are configured. Candidates say 'a blank pane with a placeholder.' When the Utilities pane has no widgets, the entire pane is hidden — the user sees no indication that it exists.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The Utilities pane in Full Case View is completely HIDDEN when no Widgets are added — it does not display an empty state or placeholder.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does a Lock icon on a Channel in the Channels landing page indicate?

options.text: The Channel component has not yet been added to the application
The Channel is restricted to administrators only
The Channel configuration is locked from editing
The Channel requires MFA to access

practiceQuiz.hint: The lock indicates an installation state, not a permission state.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The lock marks a component not yet added to the application.

optionExplanations.A: The lock marks a component not yet added to the application.
optionExplanations.B: It is not the administrator-only permission indicator described here.
optionExplanations.C: It indicates availability, not a configuration edit lock.
optionExplanations.D: It is not an MFA requirement indicator.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the Case Life Cycle, you associate the HR Worker Persona with a Web Channel and a Mobile Channel. What is the effect on the HR Worker's Channel access?

options.text: The lifecycle association does not configure the Persona’s Channel access
The HR Worker is restricted to only Web and Mobile Channels
The HR Worker is granted exclusive access to those two Channels
The HR Worker is removed from all other Channels automatically

practiceQuiz.hint: Case lifecycle Persona-Channel drafting is documentation, not access configuration.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Lifecycle drafting does not configure access; use Portal configuration.

optionExplanations.A: Lifecycle drafting does not configure access; use Portal configuration.
optionExplanations.B: Drafting the association does not restrict access to those Channels.
optionExplanations.C: The lifecycle label does not grant exclusive Channel access.
optionExplanations.D: The drafting action does not remove other Channel access.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Constellation Portal type is designed for professional users completing complex, collaborative workflows requiring in-depth data analysis?

options.text: Standard work Portal
Self-service Portal
Analytics Portal
Dashboard Portal

practiceQuiz.hint: One type is for professionals; the other is minimalistic for simple tasks.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Standard work supports the described professional workflows.

optionExplanations.A: Standard work supports the described professional workflows.
optionExplanations.B: Self-service favors simpler, occasional goal-oriented tasks.
optionExplanations.C: Analytics Portal is not one of the two named types here.
optionExplanations.D: Dashboard is a landing-page type, not the requested Portal type.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the default visibility setting when you CREATE A NEW dashboard?

options.text: Private
Public
Shared - Users with Access
Inherited from the Portal

practiceQuiz.hint: New dashboards start with the most restricted visibility.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A new dashboard starts with Private visibility.

optionExplanations.A: A new dashboard starts with Private visibility.
optionExplanations.B: Public is available, but is not the new-dashboard default.
optionExplanations.C: Shared is a configured choice rather than this default.
optionExplanations.D: The source states Private, not inheritance from the Portal.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You copy an existing dashboard that has Public visibility. What visibility does the copied dashboard have?

options.text: Public — inherits the source dashboard's visibility
Private — copies always reset to Private
Shared - Users with Access
Undefined until manually configured

practiceQuiz.hint: A copied dashboard retains source visibility; a new dashboard starts Private.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A copy retains the source’s Public visibility.

optionExplanations.A: A copy retains the source’s Public visibility.
optionExplanations.B: Private is the new-dashboard default, not a reset on every copy.
optionExplanations.C: The copy retains Public rather than automatically becoming Shared.
optionExplanations.D: Visibility is retained; it is not initially undefined.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which widget is available in both Portal landing pages AND the Full Case View, and provides team collaboration for posts, comments, and attachments?

options.text: Pulse
To do
App announcement
Case History

practiceQuiz.hint: This widget is a team communication and collaboration tool.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pulse supplies collaboration in both stated locations.

optionExplanations.A: Pulse supplies collaboration in both stated locations.
optionExplanations.B: To do lists work items rather than supplying the described collaboration.
optionExplanations.C: App announcement supplies welcome content rather than team discussion.
optionExplanations.D: Case History does not describe the collaboration tool requested.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which THREE Widgets appear on the Home landing page in the v3 source example?

options.text: Pulse
To do
App announcement
Case History

practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the three Widgets illustrated on Home, rather than assuming a universal configuration.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pulse appears in the source’s Home example. To do appears in the source’s Home example. App announcement is the third illustrated Home Widget.

optionExplanations.A: Pulse appears in the source’s Home example.
optionExplanations.B: To do appears in the source’s Home example.
optionExplanations.C: App announcement is the third illustrated Home Widget.
optionExplanations.D: Case History is not one of the three Widgets in this Home example.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What happens to the Utilities pane in the Full Case View if no widgets are configured for it?

options.text: It is hidden
It shows an empty placeholder message
It shows the Case History widget by default
It shows the Pulse widget

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish having no configured Widgets from a Widget whose data happens to be empty.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The pane is hidden when no Widgets are configured for it.

optionExplanations.A: The pane is hidden when no Widgets are configured for it.
optionExplanations.B: An empty placeholder is not the stated no-Widgets behavior.
optionExplanations.C: Case History is not automatically added by this condition.
optionExplanations.D: Pulse is not automatically added by this condition.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You want to customize the Aries theme in Constellation. What must you do first?

options.text: Save it under a new name
Copy it to the Enterprise layer
Unlock it from the Themes landing page
Convert the theme to design tokens

practiceQuiz.hint: Save the ready-to-use theme under a new name before customization.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Save under a new name before customizing a ready-to-use theme.

optionExplanations.A: Save under a new name before customizing a ready-to-use theme.
optionExplanations.B: An Enterprise-layer copy alone does not replace the naming requirement.
optionExplanations.C: The source prescribes saving under a new name, not unlocking.
optionExplanations.D: Design tokens do not replace saving the theme under a new name.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the source’s shared design-system guidance, what is the Enterprise layer also called?

options.text: Center of Excellence (COE) layer
Application Foundation layer
Design System layer
Constellation Core layer

practiceQuiz.hint: Enterprise layer and Center of Excellence layer are two names for the same concept.
practiceQuiz.rationale: COE is the alternate layer name in this source.

optionExplanations.A: COE is the alternate layer name in this source.
optionExplanations.B: Application Foundation is not the alternate name given here.
optionExplanations.C: Design System describes its purpose, not the stated alternate name.
optionExplanations.D: Constellation Core is not the alternate name given in the source.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is customizing the look and feel of a Constellation portal and needs to understand what design tokens control. What is the purpose of design tokens in Pega Constellation applications?

options.text: Store component styling in one place so the system auto-generates platform-specific styling for consistency
Define access control for UI components across Access Groups
Replace When Rules for dynamic UI behavior
Manage channel-specific layouts for mobile and desktop separately

practiceQuiz.hint: Tokens centralize styling; they do not configure access or conditional behavior.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Tokens centralize styling and generate platform-specific styling.

optionExplanations.A: Tokens centralize styling and generate platform-specific styling.
optionExplanations.B: Tokens define styling rather than Access Group permissions.
optionExplanations.C: Tokens do not replace conditional behavior or When Rules.
optionExplanations.D: The pattern supports consistent styling rather than independent layouts.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A new Persona is created in App Studio. What is automatically created in Dev Studio?

options.text: A corresponding Access Group
A corresponding ARO for all Case classes
A corresponding Channel interface
Nothing — App Studio and Dev Studio are independent

practiceQuiz.hint: Persona in App Studio → Access Group in Dev Studio.
practiceQuiz.rationale: App Studio Persona creation creates its corresponding Access Group.

optionExplanations.A: App Studio Persona creation creates its corresponding Access Group.
optionExplanations.B: The source does not say it creates an ARO for every Case class.
optionExplanations.C: Persona creation does not automatically create a Channel interface.
optionExplanations.D: The corresponding Access Group demonstrates the studio relationship.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer is explaining the relationship between Channels and Portals in Pega Constellation to a stakeholder. Which TWO statements are correct?

options.text: A Channel interface defines the delivery mechanism (web, mobile, chat) through which users interact with the application
A Portal is the web-based Channel interface through which Constellation application users access the app in a browser
Every Channel, including Email and messaging, is a web Portal
Each Pega application supports exactly one Channel interface and cannot serve both web and mobile simultaneously

practiceQuiz.hint: Channels define how the app is delivered; a Portal is one type of Channel — web browser delivery.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Channels provide interaction surfaces such as web, mobile and chat. A Portal is a web-based Channel for browser access.

optionExplanations.A: Channels provide interaction surfaces such as web, mobile and chat.
optionExplanations.B: A Portal is a web-based Channel for browser access.
optionExplanations.C: Email and messaging Channels are not all web Portals.
optionExplanations.D: Applications can provide multiple Channels, not exactly one.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO approaches match the source’s guidance for consistent Constellation branding across applications?

options.text: Share an Enterprise design system and copy its theme into a higher Ruleset when an application needs specialization
Configure application themes in App Studio and use shared design tokens for consistent component styling
Manually set color, font, and logo on every individual View and widget to ensure consistency across all Portals
Inject a custom CSS file directly into the Pega database using a system administration script

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish shared design-system reuse from theme inheritance, which is unsupported.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Shared design systems support reuse; specialize a theme with a higher-Ruleset copy. Application theme configuration and shared tokens support consistent styling.

optionExplanations.A: Shared design systems support reuse; specialize a theme with a higher-Ruleset copy.
optionExplanations.B: Application theme configuration and shared tokens support consistent styling.
optionExplanations.C: Manual styling of every View defeats centralized design-system reuse.
optionExplanations.D: Database injection is not the theme-configuration approach in this source.

quickRecap.value: Component not yet added to the application — not a permission lock.
Does NOT configure Channel access. Default: Persona has access to ALL pages.
Standard work (complex workflows, collaboration) vs Self-service (minimalistic, guided, simple tasks).
New = Private. Copy = inherits source visibility. Options: Private, Shared-Users with Access, Public.
The v3 source illustrates Pulse + To do + App announcement; configured Portals may differ.
Hidden when no Widgets are configured. Source Utilities examples include Attachments, Case operator, Tags, GenAI Coach, Followers, Prediction, Stakeholders and Related Cases.
Pegasus, Aries, Self-Service, Bootes — save under new name to customize.
Shared design system for reuse. Themes do not support inheritance; share tokens or specialize with a higher-Ruleset copy.
